S17.01.note: The model name comes from answeredByLabel in MessageBubble.tsx; the sr-only headings "You said:" and "Assistant said:" are for assistive tech only.
steps: Send any question in a new chat and wait for the answer.
Click the "More message actions" button under the answer.
Look at the label at the top of the menu: it should name the model that answered, and the answer should look different from your own message.
S17.01.where: Any answer > the "More message actions" button (the three dots under the answer). The top of that menu shows which model answered.

S17.02.note: No single control; the streaming render is in MessageBubble.tsx and useChatStream.ts. Not verified in a browser.
steps: Send a question that needs a longer answer.
Watch the answer area while it is being written.
Check that text appears in pieces as it arrives and that markdown (bold, lists, code) is formatted once it shows.
S17.02.where: Shown automatically while an answer is being written; there is no control for it.

S17.03.note: The announced status is set in ChatMessageList.tsx; I did not confirm the screen-reader announcement itself.
steps: Send a question and look at the answer area right away.
Check for the "Preparing" or "Generating response…" text before text appears.
S17.03.where: Shown automatically between sending and the first text: the wait shows "Preparing", then "Generating response…".

S17.04.needs: a model that returns reasoning (which models do this depends on the plan)
S17.04.note: The row only appears when the model returns reasoning. The expand control has the aria-label "Expand reasoning" in the same file.
steps: Use a model that shows reasoning and send a hard question.
Find the "Thought process" row under or above the answer.
Click the row and check that the reasoning text and step summary open, and that clicking again closes it.
S17.04.where: An answer that has thinking > "Thought process" row (or "Thought for <time>") > click to expand.

S17.05.needs: a prompt that makes the assistant call a tool
steps: Send a question that needs a tool, for example a question that needs a web search.
Find the "Used tools" section on the answer.
Open the section and check each tool's name, its status and its result.
S17.05.where: An answer that used a tool > "Used tools" section above the answer text ("Used N tools" when there are several).

S17.06.needs: a prompt that triggers a web search
S17.06.note: Marker behaviour is in MessageBubble.tsx and the citation helpers; I did not confirm the exact hover text.
steps: Send a question that needs current web information.
Find the small numbered markers inside the answer text.
Click or hover a marker and check that it names the source and opens its link.
S17.06.where: An answer that used web sources > numbered citation markers in the text > click a marker.

S17.07.needs: a prompt that uses web sources
S17.07.note: While the answer is still streaming the control reads "View N sources so far". The control component is SourcesControl in apps/web/features/chat/components/research/ResearchPanel.tsx.
steps: Send a question that uses web sources and wait until the answer finishes.
Find the "View N sources" control at the bottom of the answer.
Click it and check that the source list opens and each source link can be opened.
S17.07.where: A finished answer that used sources > "View N sources" control at the end of the answer.

S17.08.needs: a prompt that makes the assistant produce a file
S17.08.note: Downloads are labelled by DELIVERABLE_DOWNLOAD_ACTION in DeliverableCard.tsx.
steps: Ask the assistant for a file, for example a spreadsheet or a text document.
Find the file card under the answer, with the file name and type.
Click "Download" and check that the file saves with the name shown on the card.
S17.08.where: An answer that produced a file > file card under the answer > "Download".

S17.09.needs: a prompt that makes the assistant create an artifact
S17.09.note: The card's aria-label is "Open artifact: <title>" and the button turns into "Hide artifact" when the panel is shown.
steps: Ask for a document, a code file or a web page.
Find the artifact card under the answer.
Click the card and check that the artifact panel opens with the artifact shown.
S17.09.where: An answer that created an artifact > "Open artifact: <title>" card under the answer > click it.

S17.10.needs: a prompt that makes the assistant create an image
S17.10.note: The image card is apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/cards/ImageToolCard.tsx, but my search found no visible button text in it, so the exact control words are unknown.
steps: Ask the assistant to create an image.
Look for the image inline in the answer.
Open or download the image from its card and check that it matches the picture shown.
S17.10.where: An answer that generated an image > the image shows inline in the answer > open or download it from the image card.

S17.12.needs: a plan and deployment that allow video generation
S17.12.note: I found the composer's exit control (aria "Exit video generation mode" in apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx) but not the exact words of the control that turns video mode on.
steps: Turn on video generation in the composer and type a short prompt.
Send it and wait for the video to appear in the answer.
Press the play control on the video, then click "Download video" and check that the video plays with controls and downloads.
S17.12.where: Composer > switch to video generation (the video mode) > send a prompt > the video plays in the answer > "Download video".

S17.13.needs: a prompt that makes the assistant build interactive answer blocks
S17.13.note: The block types come from apps/web/lib/services/answer-ui-tool-service.ts; I did not find fixed visible words for the blocks.
steps: Ask for options laid out as cards or a choice list, for example "show my options as cards with buttons".
Find the cards in the answer.
Click a choice or button and check that the answer responds in place.
S17.13.where: An answer that shows interactive blocks (cards with choices, tables, buttons) > operate them inside the answer.

S17.14.note: The setting is off by default in ChatMessageList.tsx (the default constant is false), so the suggestions do not show until the switch is turned on. The deploy-level switch-on noted in the plan was not re-checked.
steps: Open Settings and go to General.
Turn on "Show follow-up suggestions in chats".
Send a question, wait for the answer, and check that suggested follow-up prompts appear below it and can be clicked.
S17.14.where: Settings > General > "Show follow-up suggestions in chats" (switch on).

S17.15.note: The aria-label changes between "Copy message" and "Message copied".
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Click the copy icon under the answer.
Paste into a text app and check that the full answer text is pasted, and that the icon briefly changes to "Message copied".
S17.15.where: Under any answer > the copy icon (tooltip "Copy").

S17.17.needs: none (a speaker is needed to hear it)
S17.17.note: The menu item is replaced by a reason text when read-aloud is unavailable; playback is in apps/web/lib/hooks/useTTS.ts.
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Click "More message actions" under the answer.
Click "Read message aloud" and check that the answer is spoken.
S17.17.where: Under an answer > "More message actions" (three dots) > "Read message aloud".

S17.18.needs: none (a speaker is needed to hear it)
S17.18.note: The unified-chat ActionBar in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/ActionBar.tsx uses the same words for other surfaces.
steps: Start read-aloud as in S17.17.
While it speaks, click "More message actions" under the answer again.
Click "Stop reading message" and check that the speech stops.
S17.18.where: Under an answer > "More message actions" > "Stop reading message" (shown while the answer is being read aloud).

S17.19.note: The aria-label is "Regenerate response" in MessageBubble.tsx.
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Click the regenerate icon under the answer (aria "Regenerate response").
Check that a new attempt replaces the answer and that the variant pager (see S17.28) now shows two attempts.
S17.19.where: Under a finished answer > the regenerate icon (tooltip "Regenerate"); with several models available it opens a menu with "Try again".

S17.20.needs: a way to make a turn fail, such as a dropped connection
S17.20.note: Retry is wired in useChatStream.ts; I did not run a failure to see the notice.
steps: Make an answer fail, for example by losing the connection during a send or by a refusal notice.
Find the "Retry" button on the failure notice.
Click "Retry" and check that the failure is replaced by a new answer for the same question.
S17.20.where: A failed answer > "Retry" button on the notice under it (aria "Retry this response").

S17.21.needs: a prompt long enough to reach the output limit
S17.21.note: The button's aria-label is "Continue generating this response".
steps: Ask for a very long answer, for example a long report.
Wait for the answer to stop part way.
Click "Continue generating" and check that the same answer carries on from where it stopped.
S17.21.where: An answer cut off by the length limit > "Continue generating" button under the answer.

S17.22.needs: an account with more than one model available
S17.22.note: The model list only appears when regenerateModelOptions has entries; the plan tier that allows it was not confirmed.
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Open the regenerate menu under the answer.
Choose a model under "Try again with" and check that a new attempt from that model replaces or joins the answer.
S17.22.where: Under a finished answer > regenerate icon ("Regenerate") > "Try again with" > choose a model.

S17.27.note: The aria-label is "Branch conversation from here" and changes to "Creating branch…" while it runs.
steps: Have a conversation with at least two exchanges.
Click the branch icon under an earlier answer.
Check that a new conversation opens with history up to that answer, and that the original conversation is unchanged.
S17.27.where: Under an answer > the branch icon (tooltip "Branch conversation: this chat stays unchanged"); also in "More message actions" on your own messages.

S17.28.needs: an answer with at least two attempts
S17.28.note: The position text is built in VariantPager.tsx as "Response {position} of {total}".
steps: Regenerate an answer (see S17.19) so it has two attempts.
Find the pager under the answer, which shows the position.
Click the next and previous buttons and check the answer changes and the text reads "Response N of M".
S17.28.where: Under an answer that has several attempts > the pager "Previous response" / "Next response" with the position text "Response 2 of 3".

S17.29.note: The rating is saved to the message through the feedback path; I did not confirm where it is stored.
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Click the thumbs-up icon under the answer.
Check that the icon shows as selected with tooltip "Remove rating", and that clicking again removes the rating.
S17.29.where: Under a finished answer > thumbs-up icon (aria "Good response"; tooltip "Good response", or "Remove rating" once rated).

S17.30.note: The details panel is ResponseRatingDetails.tsx; I did not confirm when it opens.
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Click the thumbs-down icon under the answer.
Check the rating is recorded on that answer (selected icon, tooltip "Remove rating") and, if the details panel opens, that it can be filled in.
S17.30.where: Under a finished answer > thumbs-down icon (aria "Bad response"; tooltip "Bad response", or "Remove rating" once rated).

S17.31.note: The toast text is set in MessageBubble.tsx; the report is sent to the feedback intake, which I did not trace further.
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Click "More message actions" under the answer.
Click "Report this response" and check the menu item changes to "Reporting…" then "Reported", with the toast "Reported. Thank you: our trust and safety team will review it."
S17.31.where: Under an answer > "More message actions" (three dots) > "Report this response".

S17.32.needs: a signed-in account with a chat that has messages
S17.32.note: The dialog's link-creation control text was not found in the code, and the answer share fallback when the system share sheet is missing was not traced.
steps: Sign in and open a chat that already has at least one question and answer.
Click the "Share" button in the top bar (on narrow windows only the icon shows; hover it to read "Share conversation").
In the "Share conversation" dialog, read the text and look for a link or workspace option that can be copied or shared.
To share one answer: hover the answer, click "More message actions", then click "Share answer".
Compare: the conversation dialog opens with its own title and a shareable link; the answer action opens the system share sheet, or shows "This answer could not be shared" if it fails.
S17.32.where: Open a chat that has messages > top bar "Share" button (its label is "Share conversation") > dialog titled "Share conversation". For one answer: hover the answer > "More message actions" > "Share answer".

S17.36.needs: a signed-in account and a finished answer
S17.36.note: The usage block appears only when the answer carries token data, so it may be missing on some answers; the cost figure and its exact wording were not traced.
steps: Sign in, send a message and wait until the answer has finished.
Hover the answer and click "More message actions".
Scroll to the bottom of the menu and read the token usage block and the duration line.
Look at the answer header: find the "Sent at" time and read the model name shown just below it.
Compare: the menu shows usage for that answer and the header names the model that answered.
S17.36.where: Hover an answer > "More message actions" > the usage block at the bottom of the menu (tokens and time). The model name shows under "Sent at" in the answer header.

labels.text: the response stopped part way through; the part that arrived is kept above.

S17.37.needs: a signed-in account and a way to drop the connection during an answer
S17.37.note: The network-drop step is an untested guess at a trigger; the code shows the reason text but not which failure produces it.
steps: Start a long answer.
While text is still arriving, interrupt the connection (for example turn off Wi-Fi briefly).
Look under the partly written answer for a row starting "Response failed:" followed by the reason.
Compare: the text that arrived stays visible above the row and the row gives the reason it stopped.
S17.37.where: In the chat transcript, under the partial answer that stayed on screen, as a row starting "Response failed:".

labels.text: The model declined to finish this response for safety reasons.

S17.38.needs: a signed-in account; a refusal cannot be forced on demand
S17.38.note: A refusal depends on the model's decision, so the tester may not be able to reproduce it on demand.
steps: Sign in and send a prompt that the safety layer is likely to refuse.
When the answer ends, look under it for the notice "The model declined to finish this response for safety reasons."
Read the "Retry" action and the report/appeal control next to it (its text was not found in the code).
Compare: the refusal is shown as its own notice, not as a normal answer or a generic error.
S17.38.where: Send a prompt the model refuses; the notice "The model declined to finish this response for safety reasons." appears under the last answer, with a "Retry" action.

S17.39.note: The stop control's visible label was not found in the code, so the tester must find it by its position in the message box.
steps: Sign in, send a message that gives a long answer.
While the answer is still being written, press the stop control in the message box.
Look for the notice "Response stopped." under the partial answer and keep the text that arrived.
Click "Try again" and compare: a new attempt for the same question replaces the stopped one.
S17.39.where: Send a message, then press the stop control while the answer is still being written. The notice "Response stopped." appears with a "Try again" button.

S17.40.needs: a signed-in account; an empty reply cannot be forced on demand
S17.40.note: The empty-reply case depends on the service returning nothing, so the tester may not be able to reproduce it on demand.
steps: Sign in and send a message.
If the reply comes back empty, look for a row starting "Response failed:" under the question.
Read the reason "no response was returned." and the "Retry" action beside it.
Compare: there is no empty answer bubble, and Retry sends the turn again.
S17.40.where: Only when a reply comes back empty: a row starting "Response failed:" with the reason "no response was returned." and a "Retry" action, shown in place of an empty bubble.
